pfas.note: Sampled under EPA's fifth Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule (UCMR5). EPA has set limits of 4.0 parts per trillion each for PFOA and PFOS, which water systems must meet within the next few years; the other three have no individual limit.

supply.lake: Kannapolis Lake, a 289-acre reservoir from Pump Station Road to Cannon Farm Road, holds 1.35 billion gallons. The City's own treatment plant turns it into drinking water.
supply.backups: Lake Don T. Howell (Cabarrus County) and Second Creek (Rowan County) can refill Kannapolis Lake when needed.
supply.interconnections: Pipes connect Kannapolis with Concord, Salisbury and Landis. About 0.3 million gallons a day comes from Concord for the Shiloh Church Road area.
supply.susceptibility_note: The state's Source Water Assessment (September 2020) rates how exposed each source is to possible pollution nearby, not the water's quality.

ibt.summary: Concord and Kannapolis may move up to 10 million gallons a day each from the Catawba and Yadkin river basins into the Rocky River basin (plus 6 from Second Creek). In 2024 they stayed within every condition; the most moved in a day was 5.36 million gallons from the Yadkin.

sewer.plant: Wastewater is treated at WSACC's Rocky River Regional plant in southern Cabarrus County (30 million gallons a day).

overflows.where: E 13th St at N Cannon Blvd

sewer.overflow_note: Each spill that reached surface water was reported to the State; crews cleaned the lines up- and downstream, removed debris, video-inspected the pipe, flushed the area, limed, seeded and strawed it.
never: Oil, grease or food scraps down any drain, even with a garbage disposal
Wipes (baby, cleaning, "flushable"), paper towels, cotton swabs or feminine products down the toilet
Hot water to melt grease down the drain
always: Let grease cool and harden, then put it in the trash in a closed container
Wipe greasy dishes with a paper towel before washing
Scrape food scraps into the trash

rates.note: Water is billed per 1,000 gallons: the first 7,000 at the lower rate, the rest at the higher one. Sewer is billed on the same water use. Customers outside city limits pay about 20% more. Stormwater is a flat monthly fee set by your home's roof and pavement area.

services.title: Smart water meters
services.text: Every meter in the City is a smart meter that reports readings automatically. In the customer portal you can watch your daily use, compare it with past months, and set alerts and budgets that help catch leaks early.

services.title: Grease (FOG)
services.text: Many sewer blockages are caused by grease. Never pour it down the drain: put it in a container with paper that will soak it up, put a lid on it, and place it in the trash. Restaurants should recycle grease and have grease traps cleaned often.

services.title: Backflow & cross connections
services.text: Irrigation systems, pools, boilers and fire lines tied into your water line need a backflow preventer so non-drinking water can't flow back into the City's pipes. BMP Compliance Group runs the City's backflow program (1-614-955-1091).

services.title: Save water
services.text: The City's tips for using less water around the house and yard. Smart meters can also show you a leak that's running up your bill.
